name: Keturah
title: Abraham's second wife
summary: Keturah was Abraham's second wife (or concubine) whom he took after Sarah's death. She bore Abraham six sons who became ancestors to several Arab groups. Her descendants were sent eastward with gifts, while Isaac remained Abraham's primary heir.

keyEvents.title: Marriage with Abraham
keyEvents.description: After Sarah's death, Abraham took Keturah as his wife, and she bore him six sons.

keyEvents.title: Bore Six Sons
keyEvents.description: Keturah bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah to Abraham. These became ancestors of several peoples.

keyEvents.title: Grandchildren and Descendants
keyEvents.description: Keturah's sons themselves had children who founded new clans, including Sheba and Dedan from Jokshan, and Epha, Ephah, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah from Midian.

keyEvents.title: Sons Sent Eastward
keyEvents.description: Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines, including Keturah's sons, and sent them eastward, away from Isaac, while he was still alive.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Keturah's sons and descendants are also mentioned in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles, confirming her place in Abraham's family history.
